hosted_note: 0185_new_client_waitlist_entries.sql APPLIED to production 2026-08-23, from application production 48f0238900c07bd5d2dfed5c1ebbd832e77fdc50 (project alhhybgqdmcdyzpybykj, Supabase CLI 2.102.0), raw sha256 663a5d826d4c9e610c3bf7ec599dea577772ba521326488add77153f39a14ffc, derived from the production blob rather than copied from console history. WHAT IT CREATES: the durable, studio-scoped new-client waitlist for WAIT-02B Stage A — public.new_client_waitlist_entries plus join_new_client_waitlist and remove_new_client_waitlist_entry. It moves the commit point for a waitlist request off the studio notification EMAIL (WAIT-01) and onto a committed database row; email becomes notification. Tenancy is structural: a NOT NULL studio FK, a studio-scoped PARTIAL unique index on (studio_id, email_normalized) WHERE status = 'waiting', and email_normalized generated STORED as lower(btrim(email)) so the duplicate rule's normalization lives at the authority that enforces it. There is NO global email uniqueness. APPLICATION ORDERING IS THE REVERSE OF 0183/0184: the code shipped FIRST and DARK (PR #629 merged to 48f02389 and deployed successfully) and only then was the migration applied, so the capability is live in code and live in schema while reachable by nobody. TIMESTAMPS ARE OPERATOR-OBSERVED CLIENT-SIDE WINDOWS, NOT SERVER-GENERATED APPLY TIMES. No server-side apply timestamp was captured and none is invented. SUPERSEDES the 0184 record as the CURRENT hosted-state record and CARRIES THE FULL CHECKSUM CHAIN FORWARD so no earlier apply record is dropped: 0184_client_budget_context_least_privilege.sql APPLIED to production 2026-08-17, from the authorized #593 head 74e41327b6909ec068619f9743e8099e5dd3c76a (project alhhybgqdmcdyzpybykj, Supabase CLI 2.102.0), raw sha256 aa110edadd459e0f11062e3904ea7ad54a54a75c31d9342b762a533ecc07694c. WHAT IT REPAIRS: 0183 stated its privilege contract as an allowlist ('authenticated gets SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE') but enforced it as a denylist (`revoke delete, truncate`). Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants the full set at create time, so every unnamed privilege survived and production carried GRANT SELECT,INSERT,REFERENCES,TRIGGER,MAINTAIN,UPDATE to authenticated, plus EXECUTE on the three new trigger functions to PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role. MAINTAIN is a PostgreSQL 17 privilege no by-name revoke list written for 0183 could have contained. Same root cause as 0129 (anon missed) and 0164 (service_role missed). 0184 REVOKEs ALL and grants back exactly three, so enumeration cannot fail again. This is the intended least-privilege result. ZERO BUSINESS-ROW MUTATION is a statement about the migration's EXECUTABLE CONTRACT, not a measured production row count: 0184 contains only begin, set local lock_timeout, one REVOKE ALL and one GRANT on the table, three REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON FUNCTION, and commit — pinned by a positive executable-statement allowlist in tests/migrations/0184-client-budget-context-least-privilege.test.ts. NO production row count was captured and none is claimed. public.set_updated_at() was DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED. It is a shared helper used by many tables since 0015 and carries the same permissive create-time default; changing it belongs to its own change with its own blast radius. That remains an open repository-wide hardening item, not a 0184 omission. BOTH 0183 AND 0184 ARE NOW FROZEN. Any further correction is a NEW migration; 0185 is available and NOT claimed.
